## Infosys (INFY) — Quick Brief

### Price & Action
**₹1,145.30** (▼2.97% yesterday) — trading near the lower end of its 52-week range (₹1,089–₹1,728). The stock is down ~29% from its 52-week high and has been under pressure alongside the broader IT pack.

### Valuation & Quality
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Market Cap | ₹4.5 lakh Cr |
| P/E (TTM) | **14.7×** |
| Forward P/E | **13.6×** |
| PEG Ratio | 2.14 |
| P/B | 4.84× |
| Dividend Yield | **4.37%** (₹50/sh) |
| ROE | **31.4%** |
| Debt/Equity | 0.10 (near debt-free) |
| Current Ratio | 1.98 |

At ~14.7× trailing earnings, Infosys trades well below its 5-year average P/E of ~22× — the stock is pricing in headwinds. Quality remains strong: **31% ROE**, near-zero leverage, and a healthy dividend yield of 4.4% [1].

### Fundamentals Snapshot
- **Revenue growth**: 6.6% YoY | **Earnings growth**: 11.8% YoY
- **Operating margin**: 20.9% | **Profit margin**: 16.4%
- **Free cash flow**: ₹3,170 Cr
- **Beta**: 0.11 (very low correlation to broader market)

### Recent Context
Indian IT stocks fell sharply yesterday after **hotter-than-expected US inflation** stoked fears of prolonged higher rates, compounded by AI-disruption concerns [2]. Infosys declared a **final dividend of ₹25/sh** with a June 10 record date [3].

### Key Levels
- **Support**: ₹1,089 (52-week low)
- **Resistance**: ~₹1,280 / ₹1,400

*A value play with a strong balance sheet, trading at a decade-low multiple — but near-term sentiment is weighed by macro (US rates, oil shock from Iran tensions) and AI-disruption narrative.* — Want a deeper value workup?
